title: Critical theta-half modular centering and Gibbs variance reduction
question: Can the theta-half Gibbs cancellation be centered in the bond Gibbs state itself, replacing the raw local second moment by a thermal variance without changing the Kubo-Mori shell, and does the finite Q3 stress reveal whether this removes the observed cutoff growth?
method: Use the actual-Q3 V=2 edge at d=3,4,5,6 and V=4 square at d=2 with all translated measured sites and selected bonds, both split orientations, signs, history adjoints, beta values and every prefix position.
Diagonalize each doubled-bond generator, construct its finite Gibbs logarithmic-mean weights, and subtract the bond Gibbs mean of the moved witness in that eigenbasis.
Check the exact variance identity Var_rho(X)=Tr(rho X^2)-(Tr(rho X))^2 and the fact that diagonal energy-gap-zero terms make the theta-half shell invariant under scalar centering.
Use the Gibbs pair inequality to check the finite bound N_(1/2)^2 <= (4/beta) Var_rho(X), rebuild the table in a non-importing independent lane, and compile Lean R372.
finding: Primary and independent lanes each pass 17002/17002 assertions over 2816 all-prefix contexts; the integrated verifier passes 114/114 and Lean R372 passes. The largest primary-independent numeric difference is 2.132e-13. Bond-Gibbs centering changes the maximum sampled local quantity from raw second moment 44.58328971021096 to thermal variance 41.64826651661874, with exact shell-centering error 0 and variance identity error at most 1.421e-14. The edge maxima by cutoff are 2.733031855844076, 3.4283208579615874, 4.703343964629605 and 41.64826651661874 for d=3,4,5,6; the square d=2 values are 1 up to roundoff.
decision_reason: Modular centering removes the bond-Gibbs scalar mode exactly and replaces the R-371 raw second-moment premise by the sharper thermal variance premise. The finite edge stress still rises sharply at d=6, so the remaining cutoff-uniform variance gate is not discharged. The idea is therefore retained as a sharper direct-D,delta-D target and an explicit finite obstruction to treating centering alone as a uniformity proof.

adversarial_review.check: The subtraction uses the same doubled-bond Gibbs weights that define the Kubo-Mori shell, not the unrelated full interacting Gibbs mean.
The finite row identity is checked as Var=second moment-minus-mean squared and Lean proves the finite weighted-sum decomposition.
Centering changes only diagonal spectral entries; the factor |lambda_i-lambda_j| is exactly zero on those entries, so the shell is unchanged.
Nonnegative Gibbs weights, pairwise |p-q|<=p+q, and nonnegative squared centered entries are checked; no sign cancellation is assumed.
The edge variance grows from 2.7330 at d=3 to 41.6483 at d=6; finite centering is not promoted to cutoff uniformity.
The weights are those of the finite doubled local bond proxy, not a proved global KMS state or thermodynamic limit.
The independent lane reconstructs the oscillator, Q3 graph, Gibbs state, witness, spectra and histories without importing the primary R372 module.
Lean R372 checks finite weighted variance and pair inequalities only; matrix spectra, trace passage, common core and limits remain executable/open.
Common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.

next_action: Prove or obstruct a source-, volume- and cutoff-uniform thermal-variance estimate on a Hamiltonian-derived common core; combine it with the R-370 frequency split only after that estimate is analytic.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite modular-centering checkpoint only. The doubled local bond Gibbs state is a proxy; variance uniformity, global KMS, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.
no_overclaim: R-372 removes only the bond-Gibbs scalar mode. Its finite edge variance still grows sharply, so no uniform Q3 or QFT conclusion follows.
